edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro. Irasci nolite sine causa fratri devoto: Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo. Hoc placuit Christo, resurgere mortuos, imo, Cum suis corporibus, et quos ignis ussit in aevo, Sex millibus annis completis mundo finito. Vertitur interea coelum tenore mutato: Comburuntur enim impii tunc igne divino. Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo. Digniores, stemmate et generati praeclaro, Nobilesque viri sub Antichristo devicto: Ex praecepto Dei rursum viventes in aevo, Mille quidem annis ut serviant sanctis et Alto, Sub jugo servili, ut portent victualia collo; Ut iterum autem judicentur regno finito. Nullificantes Deum, completo millesimo anno, Ab igne peribunt, cum montibus ipsi loquendo. In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto, Demerguntur inferno, trahunt poenas in aevo. Ostenduntur illis, et legunt gesta de coelo Memoria prisca debito et merita digno. Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno. Omnia non possum comprehendere parvo libello. Curiositas docti inveniet nomen in isto.
pass_a_gloss: Inhabitants of future heavens with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Simplicity, goodness, let it dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother: for you will receive whatever you do from him. This pleased Christ, to resurrect the dead, indeed, with their bodies, and those whom fire has burned in the age, six thousand years completed the world ended. Meanwhile the heaven is turned with changed tenor: for the wicked are burned then by divine fire. The creature groans, the wrath of highest God burns. More worthy, of noble stem and born, and noble men under Antichrist defeated: living again from God's command in the age, for a thousand years so that they serve the saints and the High, under servile yoke, so that they carry provisions on their neck; so that they are judged again the kingdom ended. Those nullifying God, the thousandth year completed, will perish from fire, with the mountains themselves speaking. All flesh is returned to the tombs and graves, they are submerged in hell, they drag punishments in the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, ancient memory and worthy merit. Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant. I am not able to comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find the name in this.

rejected: with the mountains testifying against them

pass_b_english: In the future heavens, God Christ will be in control from the beginning, watching over everything from heaven. We should strive to have simplicity and goodness dwelling in our bodies. There's no excuse for losing your temper with a devoted brother - you'll reap what you sow. Christ wants to bring the dead back to life, and that includes people who were burned by fire, all of which will happen once the six thousand years are up and the world as we know it comes to an end. Meanwhile, the heavens will be transformed, and the wicked will face divine fire. The creature will groan under the wrath of the highest God. Those who are more worthy, born of noble lineage, and the noble men who defeat the Antichrist will live again by God's command, serving the saints and the Most High for a thousand years, during which time they'll be subject to a servile yoke, forced to carry their own provisions, and ultimately face judgment again when the kingdom ends. When the thousandth year is complete, those who reject God will perish in fire, and even the mountains will speak out against them. Every last person will return to the grave, dragged down to hell to suffer punishment for eternity, their deeds laid bare for all to see, judged on their merits. The reward for their actions will be meted out in perpetuity, a tyrannical justice. The truth is, it's impossible to capture everything in a small book, but the curious and learned will uncover the truth hidden within these words.

review.notes: Pass B introduces significant interpretive additions and shifts in agency/modality not present in the Latin source. 1. 'God Christ will be in control' (Pass B) vs 'cum Deo Christo Tenente principium' (Latin/Pass A: 'with God Christ holding the beginning'). 2. 'We should strive to have' (Pass B) is an addition to the imperative 'Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro' (Pass A: 'Simplicity, goodness, let it dwell in your body'). 3. 'you'll reap what you sow' (Pass B) is a paraphrase of 'Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo' (Pass A: 'for you will receive whatever you do from him'). 4. 'the noble men who defeat the Antichrist' (Pass B) reverses the Latin 'sub Antichristo devicto' (Pass A: 'under Antichrist defeated'). 5. 'a tyrannical justice' (Pass B) is a significant departure from 'Merces... tyranno' (Pass A: 'Reward... to the tyrant').
reasons: Pass B adds 'We should strive to' to the imperative 'habitet'.
Pass B changes 'sub Antichristo devicto' (under Antichrist defeated) to 'noble men who defeat the Antichrist', reversing the relationship.
Pass B adds 'as we know it' to 'mundo finito'.
Pass B adds 'uncover the truth hidden within these words' to 'inveniet nomen in isto'.

review.notes: source: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. English: Inhabitants of future heavens with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven.
